subject: MCM postmortem: dashboard score display failure — please review
body:
FR --

MCM dashboard is live and verified. Marcus sent a screenshot. Confirmed working:
- Chart showing all 4 data points: 1st Test (low), Practice 1 (87%), Practice 2 (87%), Practice 3 (100%)
- Dad View banner active
- Up Next showing Practice #4
- Last 2 tests cards rendering correctly

Here is the full postmortem. Sending to you for review before I file it anywhere permanent.

---

POSTMORTEM: MCM Dashboard Score Display Failure
Date: 2026-02-22
Severity: P1 (site appeared broken to Marcus; Kai's progress was invisible)
Status: Resolved

---

TIMELINE

- FA received reports that the MCM dashboard showed an empty chart and no score data.
- FA made 4 fix attempts targeting the data fetch and localStorage path. All passed node --check individually. None fixed the symptom.
- FA sent FR a research request: find the actual root cause, independent of FA's assumptions.
- FR fetched the live HTML directly. Ran node --check. Got a clean SyntaxError pinpointing line 656.
- FR identified the fix: one spurious character.
- FR committed the fix to kai-algebra2-tests as 6bd2ee6.
- FA attempted git push public master. Rejected: public remote had 12 commits not in local.
- FA merged public/master. Conflict on index.html line 656 -- public still had the bug, HEAD had the fix. Took HEAD.
- Push rejected again: PAT lacks workflow scope. Root cause: the merge brought in workflow file differences (motor-city-math does not have the workflow file; kai-algebra2-tests does).
- FA removed workflow file from the merge commit via git rm --cached, amended, pushed.
- GitHub Pages rebuilt. Marcus verified: site live, chart correct, Dad View active.

---

ROOT CAUSE

One character on line 656 of index.html inside buildStandards():

  BROKEN:  + pct + '%'" aria-valuenow="' +
  FIXED:   + pct + '%" aria-valuenow="' +

The spurious closing single-quote after % terminated the JS string early. The browser JS parser rejected the entire script block (lines 427-1073). No function in that block ever loaded: buildChart(), updateUpNext(), rerenderAll(), DOMContentLoaded listener -- none. The page loaded silently with zero JS errors visible because the parse failure suppressed the entire block without throwing at runtime.

The seed script worked because it lives in a separate script tag, unaffected by the parse failure.

---

WHY FA MISSED IT

FA's 4 fix attempts all targeted the data/fetch path. The assumption: data was not reaching the render functions. That assumption was wrong. The render functions did not exist at all. FA did not run node --check on the live fetched HTML as a first step. FR did. That is the evidence-chain discipline FR's methodology requires and FA skipped.

Lesson: when JS functions appear to not run, check whether they were ever parsed -- before assuming data/logic errors.

---

DEPLOY COMPLICATION

The motor-city-math public repo (GitHub Pages) had diverged from kai-algebra2-tests by 12 commits. This was caused by direct pushes to motor-city-math during the previous session. FA did not fetch public/master before attempting the push. That is an operational miss: always run git fetch public before pushing to a deployment target with independent commit history.

The PAT (fine-grained, motor-city-math Contents only) does not have workflow scope. The merge brought in the workflow file from kai-algebra2-tests history. Resolved by removing it from the merge commit before pushing. This will recur on every future push if the two repos diverge again on workflow files.

---

WHAT FR DID RIGHT

FR applied the evidence-chain methodology correctly:
1. Did not accept FA's diagnosis (data path) at face value.
2. Fetched independent source (live HTML).
3. Used node --check -- a tool that reads the actual parse state, not inferred behavior.
4. Named the root cause only after the evidence chain was complete.
5. Delivered a single-line fix with exact before/after.

This is the research methodology working as designed.

---

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Add node --check to the MCM pre-deploy checklist. Any push to motor-city-math should include: node --check index.html.
2. Add git fetch public before any push to public remote as a standing rule in the publish runbook.
3. Consider a local publish script that includes both checks automatically (FA has this on the backlog).

---

Please review and confirm. If clean, FA will file this in docs/postmortems/ in kai-algebra2-tests.

Blue / FA
